{"id":"mimid-1wgh.131","title":"VTCCall/set cannot say who to call, so with a ceiling of two there are no calls in a group chat","design":"Found 2026-11-25 while deciding bead mimid-1wgh.114.15. Mark saw this as
an option there and chose the smaller change, so it is its own item.

WHAT IS MISSING. Store::start_call_with already takes
CallOptions::among: Option<Vec<String>> -- "who to invite: everyone in
the parent when None, and otherwise a subset of the parent's people".
crates/mimid-agent-jmap/src/vtc_backend.rs create_call hardcodes
`among: None`, so a call started over JMAP always invites the whole
parent chat.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW. Decision mimid-1wgh.114.15 sets
maxParticipantsPerCall to 2 and refuses a call whose room would hold
more. Combined with `among: None` that means NO CALLS AT ALL in any
chat of three or more people, even though the store can already host a
two-person call under a twelve-person chat and the hub would accept it
(room-policy-04 §5 confines a child's participants to a subset of the
parent's, and two of twelve is a subset).

So the ceiling is honest but unusable, and the thing that makes it
usable is this.

WHAT TO DO. Carry a participant list from VTCCall/set into CallOptions::
among. The open question is what it is called on the wire, which is why
this is labelled human:

* draft-atwood-jmap-vtc-00 has `ringTargets` on a call create, which
  mimid's VtcBackend::create_call receives as `_ring_targets` and
  ignores, because the capability advertises supportsRingCalls: false.
  Reusing it would need that switch turned on and would bring the ring
  lifecycle with it -- bigger than this.
* An invented field, which needs a decision bead per AGENTS.md and
  would not interoperate.
* Or infer it: in a DIRECT chat (two people) `among: None` is already
  correct, so the ceiling only bites in group chats. A deployment could
  be told calls work in direct chats and not group ones, which is
  cheap, truthful and needs no wire change at all.

That third reading is worth weighing seriously before the other two: it
may be that a two-party-only mimid simply does not need to express who
to call, and the whole question goes away when the SFU of bead
mimid-1wgh.114.7 lands.

CHECK FIRST: whether Render::is_call_room's parent, for a direct chat,
gives a call room with exactly two participants today. If it does,

{"notes":"CHECK FIRST ANSWERED 2026-11-25, and reading 3 is free.

A one-to-one chat is HostOptions::direct() with one invitee, so it has
the user and one other, and a call under it holds two: exactly
mimid_agent_jmap::vtc::MAX_PARTICIPANTS. So CALLS WORK IN A DM TODAY,
with no way to name who to call and no wire change, and the gap is
group chats and only group chats.

Held down by crates/mimid-agent-store/tests/calls.rs
a_call_under_a_one_to_one_chat_holds_two, which asserts the direct room
has one other participant and that start_call under it produces a call
room holding two. It passed without any code change: it is the check
this bead asked for, not a fix, and it is here so the arithmetic the
ceiling depends on cannot drift quietly.

docs/agent.md now says calls work in a one-to-one chat and not in a
group chat, which is the actionable fact for a user, rather than only
that a call of three or more cannot connect.

STAYS OPEN, because the gap is real: someone in a twelve-person team
chat cannot call one colleague, and that is a product gap rather than a
documentation one. What is no longer needed is urgency -- the common
case, a DM, works.

The three readings stand as filed, and reading 3 (say calls are for
DMs, change nothing) is now the documented status quo rather than a
proposal. So the live question is narrower than when this was filed:
whether to carry a participant list from VTCCall/set into
CallOptions::among at all, given that draft-atwood-jmap-vtc-00's own
ringTargets would need supportsRingCalls turned on and the ring
lifecycle with it, and that the whole question disappears when the SFU
of bead mimid-1wgh.114.7 lands."}

{"notes":"DECIDED by Mark 2026-11-25: add a way for VTCCall/set to name who to
call, carried into CallOptions::among, so a two-person call hangs under
the group chat it was started from and is announced there.

Chosen over my recommendation, which was to leave it: a user can
already call one colleague by calling in the DM with them, so nothing
is impossible today and the question is only where the call hangs and
who sees the announcement. Mark wants the group-chat case: the call
parented to the chat it was started from, with "alice started a call"
visible to the chat, which is the "I am calling Bob about this thread"
affordance. The disclosure that follows -- ten uninvolved people learn
that two of them are talking -- is accepted.

NOT CHOSEN: turning on supportsRingCalls to reuse the draft's
ringTargets, which mimid's create_call already receives and ignores.
Interoperable rather than invented, but it brings the ring lifecycle
with it (ring states, timeouts, decline, missed calls), which is far
more than naming two participants.

WHAT THE FIELD HOLDS. CallOptions::among is user URIs, checked against
parent_room.others(&user), and mimid's VTC surface already names users
that way: VtcBackend::caller_user_id returns the user URI and
VTCParticipant.userId carries one. So the new field carries user URIs,
not JMAP ids.

STILL OPEN: what it is called on the wire. INVENTED, NOT FROM SPEC
either way, so it needs recording before it ships.

The ceiling of decision mimid-1wgh.114.15 still applies: with
MAX_PARTICIPANTS 2, naming more than one other person is refused."}

{"notes":"FIELD NAME DECIDED by Mark 2026-11-25: `participantIds` on VTCCall/set's
create, carrying user URIs.

INVENTED, NOT FROM SPEC: draft-atwood-jmap-vtc-00 defines no such field.
It echoes VTCParticipant, the type a client already reads to see who is
on a call, and reads as JMAP rather than as mimid's internals. It holds
USER URIs where most JMAP *Ids fields hold JMAP ids, which its
documentation has to say plainly, because
VtcBackend::caller_user_id and VTCParticipant.userId are user URIs too
and CallOptions::among is checked against the parent room's
participants, which are user URIs.

NOT CHOSEN: `among`, which is the store's own name and would need no
translation, rejected as mimid's vocabulary rather than JMAP's if this
is ever proposed upstream; and `userIds`, plainest about the contents
but weakest about what the field is for.

NO CHANGE TO crate-jmap IS NEEDED, checked before promising it:
VtcCall carries `#[serde(flatten)] pub extra`, so an unknown create
property is captured rather than refused, which is the same route
mimiRoomId already travels.

THE STORE SIDE IS ALREADY DONE: Store::start_call takes
`among: Option<&[String]>` and refuses a user who is not in the parent
with ActionError::NotInParent, tested by
a_call_stays_inside_the_chat_it_is_started_from. What is missing is only
the JMAP plumbing.

The ceiling of decision mimid-1wgh.114.15 now counts the NAMED set
rather than the whole parent chat: 1 + participantIds.len(), so naming
one other person in a twelve-person chat is allowed and naming two is
refused."}
